findings.breaking_input: Emit of run.completed fails (spine unwritable, --strict rejection). The new line calls emitSpend(money.groups, "") with an empty run_ref, so cost.incurred rows are written naming no run.
findings.why: With no receipt written, the money row has an empty run_ref. spend-trace only checks run.completed rows, so the orphan money row is never traced. It is booked spend attached to no run, and the idempotency key built from run_ref and currency (cost.incurred|<run_ref>|USD) collides across every failed-emit run, so the second failure is deduped away as DUP_IDEM and its spend is lost silently. The diff also uses `money` in a scope not shown to be in emitRun.
findings.fix: On a failed run.completed emit, do not emit cost.incurred with an empty run_ref. Either skip it and print the unbooked figure loudly, or key the row on a fresh run id and mark it orphaned. Add a fixture where the emit fails.
findings.twin_of: A sidecar write before die() with no guard

findings.breaking_input: The CLI exits non-zero. execFileSync's e.stdout is a Buffer unless an encoding was set, and stdout may be huge or truncated by maxBuffer. A truncated or multi-line stream is parsed with a single JSON.parse.
findings.why: If stdout is truncated by maxBuffer (ENOBUFS), JSON.parse fails, failed is null, and the paid session is silently read as free. In the stream-json case on the json path the document may hold more than one line. The spend is dropped without a mark, the same class as 'spend dropped when the answer is judged bad'. A cap that cut the output also isn't named.
findings.fix: When the failure is ENOBUFS or the parse fails, record spend_absence as not-reported on the failure explicitly (arcCost with value undefined) so it reads as unproven, and try the last non-empty line.
findings.twin_of: Bytes dropped silently past a cap

findings.breaking_input: Stream path: the CLI is killed by the watchdog or the run deadline after a result event was printed, so exited.signal is set; `result` is the already-parsed final event carrying total_cost_usd, or null if the kill came before it.
findings.why: withSpend attaches spend to the failure whenever the envelope has the field. A result event that arrived but was truncated mid-line is not parsed, so the spend is dropped. A kill before the result event loses the spend of a session that did spend, and a deadline kill reads as free. The overflow branch right above returns with no withSpend even when result exists.
findings.fix: Apply withSpend to the overflow rejection too, and on kill without a result mark the failure as spend-unknown rather than leaving the field off.
findings.twin_of: Spend dropped when the answer is judged bad

findings.why: The regex tests hostname with (^|\.)openrouter\.ai$ and so rejects both of these, but ARC_LLM_SPEND=openrouter is a free opt-in that is read at any value of the endpoint, including a local proxy that reports usage.cost in other units. It then books that figure as measured USD. The owner declaration is unvalidated beyond a string compare and is read once at import, so a stale env value changes accounting for a different endpoint.
findings.fix: Record the opt-in basis on the receipt (declared versus host-matched) so a declared gateway's figure is labelled, and require ARC_LLM_ENDPOINT to be set when the opt-in is used.
findings.twin_of: A provider-specific request field sent to any endpoint

findings.breaking_input: node spend-trace.mjs --json --spine (the flag last), or `--spine=/path` (equals form)
findings.why: `--spine=/path` starts with `--` and is not in the allow-list, so it exits 2 as unknown, which is fine. But `--spine` as the last argument gives named undefined and is caught. A repeated `--spine a --spine b` uses only the first, and the second path b is never validated, so a typo there is silently ignored. Also existsSync accepts a plain file as a spine, which query then reads as a directory with an uncaught error rather than exit 2.
findings.fix: Reject a repeated --spine, and require the path to be a directory (statSync(...).isDirectory()) before querying; wrap query in try so an exception exits 2.
findings.twin_of: A flag taken as a path
